{{Quote|There is no place more sacred to the Jedi.|Jedi Padawan Ahsoka Tano, regarding Ilum's Crystal Caves|<ref name="Gathering" />}}
'''Ilum''', also later referred to as '''Starkiller Base''' due to the [[First Order]] [[Starkiller Base|military installation]] of the same name located on the [[planet]], was a [[Water|snow]]-covered [[planet]] located in the [[7G sector]] of the [[Unknown Regions]], originally located within the [[Ilum system]]. While in the [[Star system|system]], Ilum was the fifth planet from its parent [[star]] [[Asar]], a [[blue dwarf]], located roughly equidistant from Asar and the [[Star system|system's]] [[Ilum system cometary cloud|cometary cloud]]. Ilum had a [[kyber crystal]]line core, and had been utilized by the [[Jedi Order]] for [[Gathering|the Gathering]], a rite of passage in which [[Jedi Initiate|Jedi younglings]] had to find and harvest kyber crystals for their [[lightsaber]]s, which had existed for thousands of [[standard year]]s.

When the Jedi Order was [[Great Jedi Purge|exterminated]] by [[Order 66|order]] of [[Darth Sidious]], the new [[Galactic Empire]] occupied Ilum and began excavating it for its vast supply of kyber crystals, which were to be used in the construction of the [[DS-1 Orbital Battle Station|first]] and [[DS-2 Death Star II Mobile Battle Station|second]] [[Death Star]]s. The over-mining of the planet caused its core, and later a massive [[Imperial Trench]], to open up along Ilum's equator.

After the fall of the Empire, its successor state, the [[First Order]], converted the massive trench into [[Starkiller Base]]: a system-destroying [[superweapon]] that was the culmination of the Empire's research into [[dark energy]] translations and [[hyperspace]] tunneling. Held in secret by the First Order, its modifications allowed Ilum to act as a mobile base and major weapons platform until it was [[Battle of Starkiller Base|destroyed]] by the [[Resistance]] in desperation after Starkiller's [[Hosnian Cataclysm|destruction of the Hosnian system]]. Following the attack, led by [[Poe Dameron]], the planet collapsed into a star that would later be named [[Solo (star)|Solo]] after the legendary [[smuggler]] [[Han Solo]], who died at Ilum.

==Description==
Ilum was a terrestrial astronomical body smaller than a [[dwarf planet]]. With a [[kyber crystal]]line core<ref name="TROS VD" /> and a frigid climate,<ref name="SWE" /> it was considered a planet despite its size.<ref name="TROS VD" /> The planet was situated in the [[Ilum system|eponymous]] [[star system]] located in a part of the [[Unknown Regions]] known as the [[7G sector]].<ref name="Ultimate" /> Ilum was an arctic world; nearly the entire planet was covered in [[Water|ice]] and snow, and was therefore inhospitable to most [[species]],<ref name="Everything">''[[Star Wars: Absolutely Everything You Need to Know]]''</ref> though it was populated with [[Sentience|non-sentient]] animals.<ref name="NoP" />

Hidden beneath Ilum's frigid surface was what came to be known as the [[Crystal Cave]]. Within the maze-like [[cave]]s grew kyber [[crystal]]s, which brought the [[Jedi Order]] to Ilum so they could harvest the crystals in a rite of passage known as [[Gathering|the Gathering]], in which Jedi [[Padawan|initiates]] harvested their crystals by attuning themselves to [[the Force]]. As such, Ilum was a holy site for the Jedi Order for centuries.<ref name="Ahsoka">[[Ahsoka (novel)|''Ahsoka'']]</ref>

Also located beneath the surface of Ilum were [[geyser]]s, formed by [[Volcano|volcanic]] activity on the planet. These geysers warmed some bodies of water under the ice and their size or duration could change due to volcanic episodes or mineral deposition. Geological formations were also present in the caves of the planet, formed over billions of [[Standard year|years]] by accumulated [[mineral]] matter, deposited from hydrothermal fluids.<ref name="JFO" />

By [[18 BBY]], the Empire had already corrupted Ilum, draining its resources dry as well as having destroyed entire parts of the planet's surface, as they were harvesting kyber crystals; the destruction was visible even from [[Realspace|space]]. When [[Great Jedi Purge]] survivor [[Ahsoka Tano]] returned to the planet, she noted that there were at least two [[Star Destroyer]]s and a [[mining]] [[Starship|ship]] in [[orbit]] around the planet. Chunks of the planet had been carved away, exposing the rock and [[magma]] that boiled up from the planet's core.<ref name="Ahsoka" />

==History==
===Discovery===
[[File:Jedi_Temple_Ilum.png|thumb|left|250px|The surface of Ilum was barren and covered in snow.]]
Ilum's recorded history began tens of [[Millennium|thousands]] of years before the [[Galactic Empire]]'s [[Proclamation of the New Order|creation]].<ref name="NoP" /> Soon after the formation of the [[Jedi]] Order on [[Ahch-To]],<ref name="TLJ VD">''[[Star Wars: The Last Jedi: The Visual Dictionary]]''</ref> a [[Unidentified Jedi scout|Jedi scout]] performed Force-assisted [[hyperspace]] navigation through [[hyperspace route]]s, taking her to the Unknown Regions. [[Gender|She]] was drawn to a powerful resonance in the Force, which brought her to Ilum. The scout reported that Ilum was devoid of any sentient life, but was rich with non-sentient animals.<ref name="NoP" />

===Jedi uses===
Survey teams were sent out later, and ultimately discovered the vast quantity of naturally-forming kyber crystals such as [[Pontite crystal|pontite]] and [[Mephite crystal|mephite]]. The Jedi Order's [[Jedi High Council|High Council]] dispatched [[scholar]]s, [[artisan]]s, and warriors to secure the planet. The Council decided that the planet should be kept secret to [[the galaxy]] at large. [[Hyperspace surveyor]]s mapped out an uninterrupted [[Metellos-Ilum hyperspace route|hyperspace route]] from the [[Core Worlds|Core World]] of [[Metellos]] directly to Ilum, and was incredibly complex. Eventually, all mentions of Ilum were deleted and it was kept from local, [[sector]]-wide, and galactic [[star map]]s. The rogue Jedi [[Deelguh]] once led his [[Deelguh's forces|forces]] in a [[Raid on Ilum (Deelguh)/Canon|raid on Ilum]], where they clashed with defenders under Deelguh's old Jedi training comrade [[Taradon]]. Taradon sacrificed himself to take out Deelguh by crashing his [[starfighter]] into Deelguh's own craft.<ref name="NoP" />

The [[Jedi Temple (Ilum)|Jedi Temple]] on Ilum remained the last sign of intelligent life on Ilum, but was almost entirely covered by ice. All other bases on Ilum were removed by the Jedi. Ilum became a bigger supplier of kyber crystals when other planets exhausted their supplies. As was tradition, a group of [[Jedi Initiate|Jedi younglings]] would travel to Ilum to build their first [[lightsaber]]s, aboard the ''[[Crucible]]'' and escorted by a higher-ranked Jedi. According to a forgotten legend, at some point [[Sith]] may have laid [[Siege of Ilum|siege]] to the world, eventually taking possession of it for a time.<ref name="NoP" />

When Jedi youngling [[Enya Keen]] visited Ilum during the [[High Republic Era]], she listened with her whole body for whatever kyber crystal would call to her as she walked gingerly through the Crystal Caves. Finally, one specific crystal called out to her from a three-meter chasm. While she sustained cuts during her trek down, she recovered the crystal, which would shine in a nearly golden-yellow light. To Keen, the light was as if the crystal was happy to finally meet her and ready to begin their journey, with Keen unsure of what that journey would entail at that time. However, she came to understand that journey was the crystal helping in her Jedi duties and communing with the Force in new ways.<ref name="Cataclysm">''[[The High Republic: Cataclysm]]''</ref>

===Clone Wars===
[[File:IlumJediTempleInterior-TG.png|thumb|right|250px|Within the Jedi Temple on Ilum, Jedi younglings would undergo a ritual known as "The Gathering" to gather a kyber crystal and craft their first lightsaber.]]
Four [[Standard month|months]] into the [[Clone Wars]], [[Jedi Master]] [[Luminara Unduli]] took a sabbatical from the fighting to take her Padawan, [[Barriss Offee]], to Ilum to help her construct a [[Barriss Offee's lightsaber|new lightsaber]]. However, [[chameleon droid]]s happened to [[Ambush at Ilum|attack]] the temple during their time on Ilum, yet the two were saved by [[Grand Master]] [[Yoda]].<ref name="Force Users">{{EncyclopediaCite|Mace Windu and Other Users of the Force}}</ref> In [[20 BBY]],<ref name="20 BBY date note">{{TCWcanondates|506}}</ref> one [[Gathering (20 BBY)|Gathering]] took place in the midst of the war. Padawan Ahsoka Tano escorted the [[youngling]]s [[Byph]], [[Ganodi]], [[Gungi]], [[Katooni]], [[Petro]], and [[Zatt]] to the Crystal Cave, where Yoda awaited their arrival. Each youngling endured different trials to retrieve their crystals.<ref name="Gathering" />

All of the younglings left Ilum aboard the ''Crucible'', where they would be instructed by the [[architect droid]] [[Huyang]] on the construction of their lightsabers.<ref name="AToS">{{TCW|A Test of Strength}}</ref>

When [[Order 66]] was initiated, the [[clone trooper]]s of the [[481st Legion]] were deployed to Ilum to eliminate Jedi survivors hiding there.<ref name="NoP" />

===Under the Empire===
{{Quote|This place feels like it was important... But now all I sense is pain. The Empire's killing this place, a little more every day.|Luke Skywalker reflecting on the state of Ilum under the control of the Galactic Empire|<ref name="Star Wars 19">[[Star Wars (2020) 19|''Star Wars'' (2020) 19]]</ref>}}
[[File:IlumJFO.jpg|thumb|left|240px|Due to over-mining by the Galactic Empire, Ilum would later sport a large trench along its equator.]]
In 18 BBY,<ref name="Date">''[[Star Wars: The Rise of Skywalker: The Visual Dictionary]]'' states the [[Galactic Empire]]'s claiming of Ilum as taking place fifty-two [[Standard year|years]] before the [[Hosnian Cataclysm|Starkiller Incident]], which ''[[Star Wars: Galactic Atlas]]'' dates to [[34 ABY]]. Therefore, the claiming of Ilum must have taken place in [[18 BBY]].</ref> the Galactic Empire laid claim to the Jedi world<ref name="TROS VD" /> after it was discovered by Palpatine's commissioned deep space expeditions of the Unknown Regions, using ancient navigational routes found in the Jedi Temple.<ref name="CL 2016" /> Invading the planet,<ref name="Building the Death Star">{{InsiderCite|170|Building the Death Star}}</ref> the Empire quickly occupied and began strip-mining Ilum<ref name="Ahsoka" /> as part of a large-scale terraforming project.<ref name="TROS VD" /> The Empire harvested the small world's abundance of energy-focusing kyber crystals for the focusing arrays of the [[Death Star]]s' [[superlaser]]s,<ref name="CL 2016" /> thus revealing magma bubbling from Ilum's core.<ref name="Ahsoka" /> The entrance to the Jedi Temple was destroyed to allow access to the crystal caves.<ref name="NoP" /> The Empire dug a massive mining ship into the world as part of the effort to gain its riches. At least two Imperial Star Destroyers stood watch over the planet.<ref name="Ahsoka" />

The Empire's mining effort did not show respect to Ilum as the Jedi had, leaving the world ravaged and making surviving Jedi despair for the loss of many kyber crystals, which no longer sang in the Force. Nevertheless, lower concentrations of crystals still existed elsewhere in the galaxy, ready for anyone who was willing to listen for their call.<ref name="Ahsoka" /> The Empire used geothermal energy from the planet's core to power their machinery and control the internal temperature of their industrial operations. Harmful byproducts were created as a result, causing destruction to Ilum's pristine ecosystem. Eventually, a large industrial equatorial trench, called the [[Imperial Trench]], was realized over the planet as part of Imperial plans,<ref name="JFO" /> replacing what were gaping cracks that struck into the planet core<ref name="Ahsoka" /> of kyber.<ref name="TROS VD" />

After his [[Jaro Tapal's lightsaber|lightsaber]] was severely damaged, the Padawan [[Cal Kestis]] [[Mission to Ilum|visited]] Ilum's Jedi Temple to find a kyber crystal in the crystal caverns of the world and build a new [[Cal Kestis' second lightsaber|lightsaber]]. Although he had problems with the [[Imperial Garrison (Ilum)|Imperial garrison]] on the planet, he was successful in his mission and able to escape the planet.<ref name="JFO" />

During the [[Imperial Era]], Imperial [[scientist]]s undertook a [[Ilum mission|mission]] to Ilum.<ref name="Rebel Rising">''[[Rebel Rising]]''</ref>

Sometime after the [[Battle of Hoth]], Jedi-in-training [[Luke Skywalker]] visited Ilum in search of knowledge about the Jedi to complete his training. However, upon seeing the Imperial presence and what they had done to the world, Skywalker changed his mind. He felt that the place had been important to the Jedi in the past, but now there was only pain. Skywalker left the place after realizing there was nothing there for him.<ref name="Star Wars 19" />

===First Order superweapon===
{{Main|Starkiller Base}}
{{Quote|This fierce machine which you have built, upon which we stand, will bring an end to the Senate! To their cherished fleet! All remaining systems will bow to the First Order! And will remember this… as the last day of the Republic!|General Armitage Hux|<ref name="Episode VII" />}}
After the [[Battle of Jakku]], a select number of "worthy" officers and personnel disappeared into the Unknown Regions and reorganized themselves into the [[First Order]]. Ilum was chosen to begin development of the Starkiller project by the First Order, and over the 30 year period they continued the excavations started by the Empire, transforming the equatorial trench into a [[superweapon]], [[Starkiller Base]], with the planet's kyber crystalline core serving as the containment field for the base's main weapon.<ref name="TROS VD" />

By [[34 ABY]], the First Order would use the Starkiller Base to destroy the [[Hosnian system]]. The [[Hosnian Cataclysm]] destroyed the [[New Republic]], and the [[Resistance]], acting on intelligence obtained from [[Finn]], a defected First Order [[First Order stormtrooper|stormtrooper]], launched an attack on Starkiller Base in an attempt to destroy the superweapon before it could fire on their base at [[D'Qar]]. Ilum was mobilized to the [[Starkiller Base system]], whose [[Unidentified star (Starkiller Base)|star]] it then drained to recharge its weapon.

[[File:StarkillerGoesBoom-BTCG.png|thumb|right|220px|After the attack on Starkiller Base by the Resistance, the planet of Ilum collapsed, forming a star.]]
With help from [[Han Solo]], [[Chewbacca]], and Finn, who arrived on Ilum to disable the shield protecting the planet, the Resistance was able to destroy the [[thermal oscillator]] that prevented the Starkiller weapon from destabilizing. The destruction of the thermal oscillator caused a chain reaction of explosions across Ilum's surface, and Ilum imploded and exploded, becoming a miniature star<ref name="Episode VII" /> which became known as "[[Solo (star)|Solo]]."<ref name="TROS VD" />

==Inhabitants==
Ilum was home to few people, with just 5,200 sentient inhabitants. Of those 5,200, 45% were support crew, 30% were temporary researchers, 20% were military, and the remaining 5% were other individuals living on-world.<ref name="NoP" /> Prior to the fall of the Republic, the planet had no permanent residents.<ref name="Gathering" />

==Locations==
Ilum's main feature was its [[Jedi temple]], hidden beneath a large cliff of ice. Beneath that temple was the planet's massive complex of crystal caves where a vast quantity of kyber crystals could be found, and the site of the Gathering.<ref name="Gathering" /> The remainder of Ilum's surface was barren, save for canyons and mountains,<ref name="NoP" /> though there were also ice fields and [[forest]]s on Ilum's surface.<ref name="VE">''[[Star Wars: The Visual Encyclopedia]]''</ref>

==Behind the scenes==
Ilum first appeared in ''[[Star Wars]]'' [[canon]] in the sixth episode of the [[The Clone Wars: Season Five|fifth season]] of the animated television show ''[[Star Wars: The Clone Wars]]'', which was titled "[[The Gathering (episode)|The Gathering]]"<ref name="Gathering" /> and aired on [[November 12]], [[2012]].<ref name="TV.com">{{TVcom|url=shows/star-wars-the-clone-wars/the-gathering-2883427|text=Star Wars: The Clone Wars - Season 5, Episode 6: The Gathering}}</ref> The planet originated in [[Star Wars Legends|''Star Wars'' Legends]], where it first appeared in the junior novel ''[[Jedi Quest: Path to Truth]]'',<ref name="Quest">''[[Jedi Quest: Path to Truth]]''</ref> which was released in [[September]] [[2001]].<ref name="Insider 54">{{InsiderCite|54|Bookshelf}}</ref> In visual media, it appeared in ''Star Wars'' Legends through Chapters 14-16 of [[Star Wars: Clone Wars Volume Two|Star Wars: Clone Wars]], which had aired on [[Cartoon Network]] in [[2004]].<ref name="CW 14">{{CW|14}}</ref><ref name="CW15">{{CW|15}}</ref><ref name="CW 16">{{CW|16}}</ref>

In the [[2019]] [[Star Wars video games|video game]] ''[[Star Wars Jedi: Fallen Order]]'', Ilum is depicted similarly to Starkiller Base.<ref name="JFO" /><ref name="Episode VII" /> This depiction also appears in the [[2017]] reference book ''[[Star Wars Super Graphic: A Visual Guide to a Galaxy Far, Far Away]]''. Additionally, the book specifies Ilum's diameter to be 660 kilometers,<ref name="Graphics" /> which is the same diameter as Starkiller Base.<ref name="CL 2016" /> The connection between Ilum and Starkiller Base was officially confirmed in ''[[Star Wars: The Rise of Skywalker: The Visual Dictionary]]''.<ref name="TROS VD" />

The script for the ''[[Star Wars: Andor]]'' episode "[[Welcome to the Rebellion]]" originally mentioned a [[senator]] for Ilum,<ref name="WttR script">{{Disney|subdomain=assets.debut|url=documents/Andor%20209%20--%20POST%20FINAL%20--%203.3.24%5B1%5D.pdf|text=Episode #209 "Welcome To The Rebellion" Script|format=PDF}}</ref> however, in the released episode, the quote was ultimately cut.<ref name="Welcome Rebellion">{{Andor|Welcome to the Rebellion}}</ref>
